mainTopic: The dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע over ניסן and תשרי: the end of the slavery, the Exodus, the future גאולה, and the date of the מבול.
overview: This amud continues the long ברייתא about which month is the month of great events. It first finishes the proof that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה. Then a גזירה שוה on the word 'burden' (סבל) shows that the slavery in מצרים stopped on ראש השנה. The Exodus itself was in ניסן, as the תורה says openly. The first opinion, רבי אליעזר, says the future גאולה will be in תשרי, learned from the word שופר. רבי יהושע says it will be in ניסן, because the night of פסח is a 'ליל שמורים', set aside for redemption since Creation. רבי אליעזר reads that verse instead as a night guarded from מזיקין. Finally the גמרא shows that both תנאים stay consistent in another argument: רבי יהושע says the מבול began in אייר through a change in nature, and רבי אליעזר says it began in מרחשון, the natural rainy season.

steps.title: Finishing the proof that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the verse from תהלים פ״א that proves יוסף left prison on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He made it a testimony in יוסף when he went out..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began on the previous amud. It quotes the end of the verse that mentions יוסף going out of prison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same psalm speaks of blowing the שופר on ראש השנה ('תקעו בחדש שופר', verse 4) and soon after mentions יוסף going out (verse 6). Because both appear together, the גמרא learns that יוסף was freed on ראש השנה. This fact becomes the base for the next proof about the slavery in מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony, a sign or decree
A longer spelling of the name יוסף
When he went out (of prison, to rule over Egypt)
'Etc.': the verse continues

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the last piece of a proof that started on the previous amud: the psalm about the שופר of ראש השנה goes on to mention יוסף.

phrases.english: He set it as a testimony in Joseph
phrases.notes: תהלים פ״א:ו׳, continuing the verses about the שופר of ראש השנה

phrases.english: when he went out, etc.
phrases.notes: יוסף going out of prison to rule

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun on the previous amud that יוסף left prison on ראש השנה.
steps.raayaObject: יוסף left prison on ראש השנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים פ״א: the שופר of ראש השנה is mentioned right next to יוסף's going out.

steps.title: The slavery in מצרים stopped on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the hard labor of our fathers in מצרים stopped on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה the slavery of our fathers in מצרים stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new fact: the forced labor in מצרים ended on ראש השנה. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different event from the actual Exodus. The work stopped in תשרי, but the Jews only left מצרים months later, in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Stopped, ceased
Labor, here the forced slave labor
From our forefathers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with יציאת מצרים. The slavery stopped on ראש השנה in תשרי, and the Exodus came about six months later in ניסן.

phrases.english: On Rosh Hashanah the labor stopped
for our forefathers in Egypt

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בָּטְלָה עֲבוֹדָה מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact that יוסף was freed on ראש השנה. That fact will be used to date the end of the slavery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slave labor in מצרים ended on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'burden'
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on the word סבל connects the burdens of מצרים to יוסף's release, so both happened on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: "I will take you out from under the burdens of Egypt," and it is written there: "I removed his shoulder from the burden."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous statement by linking two verses that both use the word 'burden' (סבל).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about יוסף ('I removed his shoulder from the burden') is in the same psalm that showed he was freed on ראש השנה. The verse about the Jews in מצרים uses the same word, 'burdens'. Through the גזירה שוה, the end of the Jews' burden is given the same date as יוסף's: ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (in our topic)
And it is written there (in the other place)
Burdens / burden: the shared word of the גזירה שוה
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: It is written here: "And I will bring you out
from under the burdens of Egypt"
and it is written there: "I removed his shoulder from the burden."

steps.raayaObject: The slavery in מצרים ended on ראש השנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה of סבל (שמות ו׳:ו׳ and תהלים פ״א:ז׳), tied to יוסף's release on ראש השנה.

steps.title: The Exodus happened in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the redemption from מצרים was in ניסן, and this needs no proof because the Torah says it openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ניסן they were redeemed, as it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states that the Jews left מצרים in ניסן. The גמרא says no special proof is needed because the Torah states it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כדאיתא' means 'as it plainly is': the Torah openly places יציאת מצרים in the month of the spring (חודש האביב), which is ניסן. So unlike the other statements, no גזירה שוה is needed here.

keyTerms.meaning: They were redeemed
As it is (plainly written), so no derivation is needed

phrases.english: In Nisan they were redeemed, as it is (explicitly written).
phrases.notes: The תורה openly says the Exodus was in ניסן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of the slavery (תשרי) to the actual Exodus (ניסן).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יציאת מצרים took place in ניסן, as the Torah explicitly states.

steps.title: The future redemption will be in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion in the ברייתא (רבי אליעזר) says the final גאולה will come in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In תשרי they will be redeemed in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states that the final גאולה will take place in תשרי. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the first redemption was in ניסן, this opinion holds that the future one will be in תשרי. This sets up the disagreement with רבי יהושע here.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future, they are destined to
To be redeemed

phrases.english: In Tishrei they will be redeemed in the future

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the past redemption (ניסן) with the future one (תשרי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first opinion, the final גאולה will be in תשרי.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'שופר'
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on the word שופר links the שופר of ראש השנה to the great שופר of the final גאולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is learned from 'שופר' and 'שופר'. It is written here: "Blow the שופר at the new moon," and it is written there: "On that day a great שופר will be blown."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the future גאולה will be in תשרי by matching the word שופר in two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Blow the שופר at the new moon' refers to ראש השנה in תשרי. 'A great שופר will be blown' refers to the final גאולה. The shared word teaches that the גאולה will come in the month of ראש השנה, which is תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from: the formula that introduces a גזירה שוה
A great shofar, the shofar of the final redemption
Blow (the shofar)

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion: the slavery stopped in תשרי (from סבל), the Exodus was in ניסן (explicit verse), and the future גאולה will be in תשרי (from שופר).

phrases.english: It is learned from "shofar" and "shofar."
It is written here: "Blow a shofar at the new moon"
and it is written there:
"On that day a great shofar will be blown."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו כ״ז:י״ג, about the final גאולה

steps.raayaObject: The final גאולה will be in תשרי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה of שופר between תהלים פ״א:ד׳ (ראש השנה) and ישעיהו כ״ז:י״ג (the great שופר of the גאולה).

steps.title: רבי יהושע: both redemptions are in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע disagrees and says both the past and the future גאולה are in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: In ניסן they were redeemed, and in ניסן they will be redeemed in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings רבי יהושע's opposing view: the future גאולה will also be in ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the Exodus was in ניסן. They argue only about the future גאולה: the first opinion says תשרי, and רבי יהושע says ניסן, the same month as the first redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהושע says: introducing the opposing view

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
In Nisan they were redeemed,
in Nisan they will be redeemed in the future

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the first opinion's claim (steps 5–6) that the future גאולה is in תשרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, the final גאולה will be in ניסן.

steps.title: Asking for רבי יהושע's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the future גאולה will be in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יהושע's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the Exodus was in ניסן is explicit, so the question is only about the future גאולה. The first opinion had a גזירה שוה, so רבי יהושע also needs a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know (this)?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהושע's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the future גאולה will be in ניסן.

steps.title: The night of watching since Creation
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'ליל שמורים' teaches that the night of פסח has been set aside for redemption since Creation, so the future גאולה will also come then.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "A night of watching." This means a night that has been watched (set aside) ever since the six days of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a verse about the night of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ליל שמורים' is read as a night 'guarded' for redemption from the beginning of the world. A night set aside for redemption since Creation was not used up by the Exodus. It stays ready for the final גאולה, so that will also come in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says: introducing a proof verse
A night of watching (the night of פסח)
Watched, guarded, set aside
The six days of Creation

steps.whatToRemember: The argument: the first opinion learns the future גאולה is in תשרי from the שופר. רבי יהושע learns it is in ניסן from 'ליל שמורים', a night set aside for redemption since Creation.
steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבי יהושע, the Exodus did not use up the night of פסח. It stays set aside for redemption, so the final גאולה is expected in ניסן.

phrases.english: The verse states: "A night of watching"
a night that is watched (set aside)
and has been so since the six days of Creation.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ליל שמורים' (שמות י״ב:מ״ב): the night of פסח has been guarded for redemption since Creation, so the future גאולה will also be in ניסן.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר reads the verse 'ליל שמורים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר understands 'ליל שמורים'. He reads it as a night guarded from מזיקין, not as a source for the future גאולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי אליעזר)? He learns from it that this is a night that is always guarded from demons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר does with the verse רבי יהושע just used. It answers that he learns a different lesson from it: on the night of פסח, מזיקין have no power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רבי יהושע read 'שמורים' as 'set aside for גאולה from long ago.' רבי אליעזר reads 'שמורים' as 'guarded and protected.' Since he uses the verse for protection, he does not need to accept רבי יהושע's proof that the future גאולה will come in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (How does the other opinion handle this verse?)
A night that is guarded and protected
Harmful spirits, demons

steps.confusionAlert: The one word 'וְאִידַּךְ' is the whole question. Do not read past it. The גמרא is asking, in a single word, what the other תנא does with this verse.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a standard pattern in the גמרא. When one side brings a verse as proof, the other side is shown to use the same verse for a different lesson.

phrases.english: And the other one (how does he use this verse)?
phrases.notes: A one-word question: what does רבי אליעזר learn from 'ליל שמורים'?

phrases.english: A night that is continuously guarded from demons.
phrases.notes: The answer: the verse is about protection, not about the date of the גאולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אליעזר reads the verse that רבי יהושע used as his proof in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'ליל שמורים', since he does not use it for a ניסן גאולה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns that the night of פסח is guarded from מזיקין.

steps.title: Both תנאים stay consistent: setting up the flood ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע follow their usual reasoning. It introduces a ברייתא about the date the flood began.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught in a ברייתא: 'In the six hundredth year of נח's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to show that the same two תנאים argue the same way in another place, the date of the מבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the flood began in 'the second month' but does not say which month comes first. The question is whether we count from ניסן or from תשרי. That is the same ניסן-versus-תשרי dispute these two תנאים have about the world's creation and the גאולה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they follow their own reasoning (they stay consistent)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
In the second month

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a parallel dispute between the same two תנאים.

phrases.english: "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life,
in the second month,
phrases.notes: Second month counted from which month? This is what they will argue about.

phrases.english: on the seventeenth day of the month."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ניסן-versus-תשרי dispute between the two תנאים appears in another topic as well.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two תנאים argue consistently about whether the year's months are counted from ניסן or from תשרי.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the flood began in אייר through a change in nature
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the flood began on 17 אייר, a dry season. Because the people changed their deeds, הקדוש ברוך הוא changed nature and brought the flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: That day was the seventeenth of אייר. On that day the constellation כימה sets during the daytime, and springs become smaller. But because the people changed their deeds, הקדוש ברוך הוא changed the workings of Creation for them. He made כימה rise during the day, took two stars from כימה, and brought a flood to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע counts 'the second month' from ניסן, so he says the flood began in אייר. Since אייר is naturally a drying season, he explains that the flood came through a change in nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבי יהושע's view that ניסן is the start of the year. It also forces him to say the flood was unnatural: water should have been decreasing at that time. The idea is measure for measure. The people changed their behavior, so הקדוש ברוך הוא changed nature.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of אייר, second from ניסן
The constellation כימה (often identified with the Pleiades)
The springs diminish
The natural workings of Creation
The flood

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying אייר is a rainy season. He says the opposite: it is a dry season, so the flood needed a miraculous change in nature.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּאִיָּיר הָיָה,
phrases.english: That day was the seventeenth of Iyar,
the day when the constellation Kimah sets in the daytime
and the springs diminish.
But because they changed their deeds,
phrases.notes: The generation of the flood acted wickedly.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁינָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהֶם מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, changed the workings of Creation for them,
and He made Kimah rise in the daytime,
and He took two stars from Kimah
and brought a flood to the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהושע's side of the ברייתא introduced in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flood began on 17 אייר (counting from ניסן) through a supernatural change in nature.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the flood began in מרחשון, the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the flood began on 17 מרחשון, when כימה rises by day and the springs naturally increase.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: That day was the seventeenth of מרחשון. On that day the constellation כימה rises during the daytime, and springs grow stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר counts 'the second month' from תשרי, so he says the flood began in מרחשון. That is a season when water naturally increases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבי אליעזר's view that תשרי is the start of the year, the same view behind his claim in step 5 that the גאולה will be in תשרי. Unlike רבי יהושע, he does not need a change in nature, because the flood fits the natural rainy season.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of מרחשון, second from תשרי
Rises during the daytime
Grow stronger, increase

steps.whatToRemember: The two תנאים are consistent. רבי יהושע counts from ניסן (creation, גאולה, and the flood in אייר). רבי אליעזר counts from תשרי (creation, גאולה, and the flood in מרחשון).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּמַרְחֶשְׁוָן הָיָה,
phrases.english: That day was the seventeenth of Marcheshvan,
the day when the constellation Kimah rises in the daytime
and the springs increase.
phrases.notes: Naturally a rainy season, so no miracle is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אליעזר's side of the ברייתא, opposing רבי יהושע in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flood began on 17 מרחשון (counting from תשרי), in the natural rainy season.
